related_questions.question: What is the highest interest rate in US history?

text_blocks.snippet: The highest interest rate in US history was the prime rate, which reached 21.5% on December 19, 1980. The Fed Funds Rate, the rate at which commercial banks lend to each other overnight, hit 20% in March 1980. These high rates were a response to severe inflation during the late 1970s and early 1980s.

text_blocks.snippet: In 2021, the Federal Reserve kept the target interest rate near zero, specifically between 0% and 0.25%, throughout the year. This was done to support the economy during the COVID-19 pandemic. While the federal funds rate remained low, other interest rates, like mortgage rates, saw significant fluctuations. Mortgage rates started the year around 2.65% but rose to around 3.15% by the end of the year.

list.title: Mortgage Rates:
list.snippet: While the base interest rate was low, mortgage rates started the year low but increased throughout 2021. The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was around 2.96% in early 2021 and rose to 3.15% by the end of the year, according to The Mortgage Reports.

list.title: Other Interest Rates:
list.snippet: The 10-year Treasury yield, which influences many loan rates, increased from around 0.93% at the beginning of the year to 1.52% by the end, according to FocusEconomics.

list.title: Reasons for the Increase:
list.snippet: This increase in some rates, despite the low federal funds rate, was partly due to concerns about inflation and the anticipation of the Federal Reserve tapering its asset purchases, according to the CFPB.
